key_insight: The paper extends Newton’s method to nonsmooth optimization by using coderivative-based generalized Hessians plus an adaptive regularization and nonmonotone line search for stable convergence.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical high-order optimization tool for machine learning and inverse/design problems with nonsmooth objectives such as Lasso and SVMs.
method: Builds Newton steps from coderivatives of the subgradient mapping (generalized Hessians).
Uses adaptive regularization to handle positive semidefinite or ill-conditioned generalized Hessians.
Adds a Hybrid Adaptive Nonmonotone (HAN) line search to improve global robustness and practical performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on Lasso, logistic Lasso, and SVM problems, showing competitive performance against established first- and second-order nonsmooth solvers.
watch_item: Performance depends on the semismooth* / regularity assumptions and the added second-order machinery may increase per-iteration implementation complexity.
paper_title: Nonmonotone Coderivative-Based Newton Methods for Nonsmooth Optimization with Machine Learning Applications
